en: Relax your mind... Clear your thoughts... Unload yourself...  This is a one-of-a-kind experience that people desperately need, especially in dark times like these.
Nah, maybe some other time. I'm broke enough as it is.
Nah, maybe some other time.
In closing, I ask you to take a look around you. If you feel like making Kineicho⑬no, all of Nagoya⑬a better place, then please vote Shozo Matsukane on election day!
This concludes my talk. Thank you all for your time and consideration!
Don't forget to vote, my friends! Sow a seed into the future!
...Wait, what the heck?
It seems that no one bothered to stick around.
Ooh, I'm sorry about that. I kept screwing up and saying the wrong things.
No, that's quite all right. I'm the one who begged you to do this. No need to apologize. That's just how things go sometimes.
So, what now? Are you going to keep going with your streetcorner speeches?
Hmm. I don't know. Doing this solo is disheartening.
Hey, boss! I'm sorry I'm so late!
Looks like someone beat me to the endorsement speech.
I wanted to go first!
Huh? What's with all these people...?
Everyone... You guys actually came to support me?
Are you kidding? Of course we did! You've been so good to me for years.
Matsukane-san, I'm sorry for being so abrupt on the phone. It took me a while to pencil in some free time.
Allow me to lend a hand as well.
I guess you're not so alone after all, are you? There goes my first impression.
It's a blessing, that's for sure. Now I really can't let you guys down.
But, Ta-chan, you were the one that was there when I was down on myself the most.
If you hadn't come through for me, I probably would have lost all hope.
Aww, why thank you. Makes me feel a little less awful about botching things up.
I'm serious, Ta-chan. I really appreciate what you did for me!
Goodness me! Look at all these people!
Keep at it!

en: Ya sure got my vote!
See you at Shachoko sometime!
If your ramen's as good as your campaign, then I'm sold!
You did it, Ta-chan! You made this a huge success!
Hehe, I kinda did, didn't I? Guess anything's worth a try.
Your endorsement speech was truly magnificent! That's some hidden talent you have.
Aww, you're too kind. Now you're just inflating my ego.
It's no flattery⑬that's some gift of persuasion you have there. Truly, I'm in your debt.
Unfortunately, I am on a campaign now, so I can't legally offer you any reward. I feel terrible about it, but⑬
Oh, no worries, man! I'm just glad I could help out.
It looks like you found someone perfect already.
Wait... You don't mean me, do you?
Who else? That was a better endorsement speech than I could have ever hoped for.
Let me take a shot at it, too. I'll try to match it just as good! And I'll put extra emphasis on how great of a manager you are!
I, too, would like to speak on your behalf.
Then make that three!
What can I say, I'm a lucky guy. I'm going to have to dig down deep so I don't let you people down.
But, Ta-chan, you're the one who really put me back on track. Thank you!
Oh, Ta-chan! Just the man I wanted to see.
You wanted to see <Italic>me</Italic>? I thought you were gonna find someone to endorse you. What happened to that?
That's just it. Nobody would come out. They all said they were too busy to help.
Ouch. Guess you're not very popular, are you? Isn't that kind of a problem for a politician?
Boy, that is really not what I needed to hear right now.
Haha, it was just a joke. Someone's gotta lighten the mood.
Ta-chan, things are getting desperate here. I hate to impose, but can you do an endorsement speech for me?
Huh? Me, give a speech? What, are you nuts? You know I can't do that.
I'm begging you, please. I'll explain my policies right now. Oh, and throw in some wonderful qualities about me as well.
Uh. Like what?
Oh, come on, there's so many. Don't you remember? When you were flat broke, I'd give you big portions for the price of a regular bowl.
Did... that ever actually happen?
Happened all the time! Come on, Ta-chan, be of some help. I simply cannot stand it anymore! Being out here alone is so... so horrible...
You don't have to cry about it, you know. No one's forcing you to do this.
Granted, yes, that's true...
Besides, who's going to listen if I do make a speech? An endorsement only works if it's someone famous.
I tried to ask people like that, but each one turned me down.
Maybe if you just start speaking with a fiery fervor, people will automatically assume you're someone famous! And then they'll stop and listen!
Yeah, doubt that.
No, I'm sure it'll happen. You're my only hope! It's either this, or my career as a politician is doomed!
Oh, all right. You've always been good to me, so I guess I owe you one. Let's see what I can do.
You mean you'll help me? Really? You're the man, Ta-chan!
Don't go expecting too much. You and I both know it's a longshot.
Duly noted.
Okey-doke. So, I should talk about what a great guy you are while simultaneously promoting your platform, right?
You don't have to put it so bluntly, but yeah, that's the gist of it.
So what is your platform, anyway?
Well, I'm an advocate of three key policies: tax cuts, job creation, and childcare support. You could say they're the three pillars of my political philosophy.
Got it. Have you thought of how you're going to achieve all that?
Of course I have. I'm not just doing this political thing on a whim. It's a bit lengthy, but let me fill you in on these policies.
First, tax cuts. My primary focus is to reduce the residence tax. We'll make up for the deficit with transfers from the national treasury.
By cutting wasteful government spending, we can systematically reduce the tax burden on all of our citizens.

That will spur consumer spending in their local communities,
which in turn will stimulate growth nationwide.
Wow. That sounds like an actual policy!
Next, job creation. This also involves tax cuts. By reducing corporate taxes in Nagoya, we'll attract more businesses to the area.
But the more money you make, the more taxes you pay. As a result, companies try to move their operations to tax havens offshore.
However, if all the rich were to flee Japan, the burden would fall on the rest of us. And eventually it would come full circle.
That's why I strongly believe reducing the tax burden on companies and the wealthy will revitalize Nagoya's economy and result in new jobs.
Okay, got it. So it's not always bad to give the rich a break. Go figure.
Third is childcare support. In order to raise the birthrate to sustainable levels, the government needs to do its part to help child-rearing families.
I'm proposing that the child tax benefit be increased, with the difference to come from higher taxes for single people.
Huh? That doesn't sound good for me.
No, it doesn't. So singles will think it's more worthwhile to raise kids. That will encourage more couples to marry.
Perhaps this may be criticized as just vote-buying, but I think the government needs to invest in the younger generation.
True, true... Okay, I think I got it all down.
I'll try to work all that into my speech somehow.
Then I'll be counting on you, Ta-chan!
Yup. So, just to recap...
Your three pillars were tax cuts, job creation, and childcare support. Huh, that about does it. Well, here goes nothing!
You're barking up the wrong tree. Sorry, but no can do.
You can't leave me like this. I can't do this by myself!
Ta-chan, please, help me out with an endorsement speech. You're the only one who can do it. Please? Don't make me beg.
Er-hem! Good day, fellow citizens! I'm sorry to disturb you on your busy day, but may I have your attention?
Is that some campaign rally?
Who is that man?
I'm sure I've seen that face before.
Maybe it's somebody famous?
My name is Tatsuo Shinada. I am here today as a representative of the common people in support of Shozo Matsukane.
Matsukane-shi has long operated a ramen restaurant in town. He can be considered a hero for filling the bellies of our fellow citizens.
Being locals like myself, I'm sure you at least know of Matsukane-shi's ramen restaurant, which goes by the name, uh...
Shachihoko Ramen! Held in the highest esteem among ramen fans in the know for its uniquely Nagoya charm.
Shachihoko?
There's a ramen place called that?
I never heard of it.
Hey, that's not it at all, Ta-chan! We're <Italic>Shachoko</Italic> Ramen. At least get that one right!
Yes! Shachoko! I've enjoyed many a heaping bowl of noodles as a regular there.
A regular wouldn't get the name wrong.
Shachoko Ramen! Held in the highest esteem among ramen fans in the know for its uniquely Nagoya charm.
Hello! I am indeed the manager of Shachoko Ramen, and I hope I may count on your support for my entry into politics.
Oh, so that's their manager!
I've been there.
They're tasty.
As a regular of Shachoko Ramen, I've enjoyed many heaping bowls of steaming noodles there.
This personable and kind-hearted manager hopes to enter politics to represent us⑬the everyday folks that keep this town afloat.
That's right! So please remember to lend Shozo Matsukane your support come election day!
Shachokehold Ramen! A ramen shop so gripping, it'll judo-slam your taste buds into submission! Ohhh yeaaahhh!
Sha...chokehold?
What, is it owned by a former wrestler?
...Yeah, no thanks.
Matsukane-shi's platform consists of three pillars!
These pillars are the policies he will make every effort to enact if you would grant him the chance to serve you in office!
The first pillar⑬tax cuts! If the financial burdens on our citizens are not reduced, the economy will remain moribund and hopeless!
Matsukane-shi pledges to reduce the residence tax that we all currently pay.
How does he propose to make up for the shortfall from the reduction in the residence tax? The answer is to...
Get transfers from the national treasury. And by cutting waste from the national budget, residence taxes in all of our communities will be reduced.
The Japanese economy cannot be revived without a real improvement in the people's standard of living throughout the country.
It is up to the local communities to inform the national government of this critical fact. I hope to be the vanguard of that movement.
I'm all for cutting taxes.
I'll be holding you to that!
This economy really does need help.
Matsukane-shi pledges to reduce your taxes as his first policy if he's given the chance to be your voice in the government!
I, Shozo Matsukane, promise to fight with my life to honor the trust you place in me! But only you can give me that opportunity!
We will stake our future on unearthing buried gold. Now is the time to find what has only been left to rumors. We want... No, we must find it!
No! Ta-chan, I would never rely on a ludicrous gamble like that!
Buried gold? That's ridiculous.
What is he thinking?
You can't bank on that.
No, that isn't it. My plan is to obtain transfers from the national treasury. There's a solid reasoning behind this approach!
But it would be pretty cool if there was hidden gold waiting to be discovered! Don't forget!
Would you drop that? Ta-chan, stick to the script, please.
Sell off city assets! We pledge to sell off everything and anything. With the proceeds we can take it easy and enjoy life!
Wait! Stop it! What are you saying? Are you out of your mind?
That's only a temporary fix.
What happens when there's nothing left to sell?
Won't the residence tax just come back?
No, that isn't it. My plan is to obtain transfers from the national treasury. I am not an advocate of any stopgap measures!
Come on, Ta-chan, you're killing me. You have to pay attention here.
Next, the second pillar of his three-fold platform⑬job creation! Something must be done about the ridiculously high unemployment!
In these tough economic times, we must reverse the shrinking job market. How is Matsukane-shi gonna tackle this?
By expanding social services! By doing so, we can boost the employment rate while also providing our seniors with even better care!
Won't that end up costing the city even more? Where's the funding coming from?
Are you going to hike up our taxes even more?
Better social services might have a nice ring to it, but it's only about throwing cash around.
Ta-chan, that's not what I said! I said reduce the corporate tax burden so we can attract more businesses to set up shop in Nagoya.
